source.title: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Cross-Modal Learning for Histology and Gene Expression in Spatial Transcriptomics
source.authors: R. Gindra; G. Palla; M. Nguyen; S. Wagner; Manuel Tran; Fabian J. Theis; Dieter Saur; L. Crawford; Tingying Peng

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-modal image–gene retrieval and reports that alignment varies with the gene encoder, dataset, and batch effects. It refines the convergence claim by showing data- and modality-specific influences, rather than testing scale-driven convergence directly.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's cross-modal image–gene retrieval results and its stated batch-effect/retrieval relationship. The downstream mutation and gene-expression prediction results are not rows because they measure downstream task performance, not representational alignment. The paper's cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: This is a benchmark of contrastive (CLIP/SigLIP) pretraining that explicitly trains histology and gene-expression encoders to align, then reports Recall@k. That alignment is induced on purpose by the training objective, not measured as arising between independently trained models. The rows compare the study's own encoder combinations. There is no scale sweep, no seed comparison, no untrained or zero-shot representational similarity measurement, and the paper does not engage the Platonic or convergent-learning claims. Its results therefore do not bear on any version. The batch-effect versus retrieval link concerns how well trained alignment succeeds, not emergent convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find gene-encoder choice (dataset-pretrained DRVI) is the main determinant of retrieval, and spatially pretrained foundation models beat single-cell ones. Contrastive pretraining improves mutation classification for some biomarkers but often degrades gene-expression prediction versus baseline image encoders. They attribute problems to batch effects and call for batch-robust multimodal methods.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains image and gene encoders with contrastive objectives and evaluates paired-data retrieval using Recall@k, rather than testing convergence through the original sources' representational-similarity procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieval differs across tissue panels and image-to-gene versus gene-to-image direction; Recall@k values change with k. The authors also report a clear relationship between batch integration and retrieval performance.

fits_no_version.finding: After CLIP-style contrastive training, histology-gene retrieval depends mostly on the gene encoder. Dataset-pretrained DRVI beats foundation models, which beat the MLP. Retrieval tracks batch integration (Silhouette Batch) across datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The success of trained cross-modal contrastive alignment in spatial transcriptomics depends on gene-encoder pretraining and on batch effects in the gene modality.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
record.problems: No model-size or capability sweep; image–gene retrieval is not the vision–language setting specified by V2. Alignment is assessed using retrieval rather than direct comparisons of representation-space distances, and the batch-effect relationship is shown in a figure without numerical effect estimates in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The benchmark reports many further model combinations and Recall@1/Recall@10 values across panels in Tables 2, 7, and 8; these were omitted to prioritize the DRVI-versus-MLP comparison, representative pretrained gene encoders, selected k comparisons, and the stated batch-effect relationship. Downstream-task tables were excluded because they do not directly measure alignment.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no comparison of independently trained models.
No vision-language pairing, and alignment is trained contrastively rather than measured between independently trained models.
No post-hoc mapping or stitching between independently trained representations. Alignment is learned end-to-end through contrastive heads.
No representational similarity measures (e.g. mutual k-NN, CKA) on independent models. Recall@k is computed after trained alignment.
Measures no emergent alignment, so it cannot show partiality or a shared-data explanation of convergence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' classification is not supported. The alignment is produced by the contrastive objective itself, which falls under 'induces the behaviour on purpose'. The paper does not cite either original source. 'cites_only' is used as the nearest relation for a T6 study; it neither tests nor uses the convergence finding.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of whether independently trained models become more aligned as they scale.
The paired modalities are histology images and gene-expression profiles, not vision and language models paired on images and captions.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations of the same architecture, shared features, or shared subspaces.
No mapping between model representations, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No study of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
The study varies Recall@k and the datasets/panels, but does not compare alternative representational similarity measures such as distance-based measures, or test out-of-distribution inputs.

The study reports data-specific encoder effects and batch-effect associations, but does not test a scale-related plateau or distinguish a common model of reality from shared objectives as a causal explanation.

rows.measure: Relationship between Silhouette Batch score and mean Recall@5
rows.note: The text describes a clear linear relationship: datasets with better batch integration have better cross-modal retrieval.
rows.check: Silhouette Batch vs mean Recall@5 (Figure 2, figure only, no numbers). It concerns data quality affecting trained contrastive alignment, not the causes of emergent representational convergence.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Recall@k metrics and the evaluated tissue panels
reader_labels.reason: Retrieval scores vary with the panel and with k; for example, the 5K and Lung scores differ at the reported k values, so measured alignment depends on input setting and retrieval cutoff (R01-R12, R46-R53).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Contrasts among dataset-pretrained DRVI, the MLP baseline, and pretrained gene encoders across panels
reader_labels.reason: The results show that dataset-pretrained DRVI generally yields higher retrieval than the MLP comparator, while the scores vary by panel; the paper also reports an association between batch integration and retrieval (R01-R24, R45).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Retrieval is incomplete and heterogeneous across panels, directions, and k settings; the study does not establish a universal or scale-driven convergence pattern (R01-R12, R46-R53).
